sections.heading: How to Play Preservation
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Preservation"][color=evoker]Preservation Evoker Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]
[pad]
Preservation Evoker is an unconventional healer with a few unique mechanics that can make it a little more daunting to pick up, but it's also extremely fun once you do. Midnight removes quite a few buttons and interactions, which should greatly improve the accessibility of the spec. Here are some core concepts to keep in mind, especially if you're new to the spec:

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_evoker_temporalanomaly size=medium type=round color=c13 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=evoker]Use Short Cooldowns Regularly:[/color][/b] Cast [spell=373861] the moment it comes off cooldown. It generates a lot of [spell=364343] buffs and heals for a decent amount via its absorb. Cast [spell=355936] regularly when you do not have [spell=364343] buffs out.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_evoker_echo size=medium type=round color=c13 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=evoker]Cast Echo:[/color][/b] Use your Essence resource and [spell=369297]s and try to avoid wasting any of either. You will mostly cast [spell=364343], but with the [spell=1242031] talent, you might weave with [spell=355913].
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_evoker_reversion size=medium type=round color=c13 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=evoker]Consume Echoes:[/color][/b] Consume [spell=364343] buffs with powerful spells like [spell=1256577] (or [spell=367364]) and [spell=355936]. More information on this choice in the rotation section.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]

[center][wrapper width=800px][box border=true]If you're looking for a more bite-sized rotation explanation, check out our simplified guide below:

[center][cta-button=guide=32619 icon=classicon_evoker_preservation]Preservation Evoker Beginner Guide[/cta-button][/center][/box][/wrapper][/center]

sections.heading: Raid Basic Priority & Rotation
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Raid Basic Priority & Rotation" type=bar][icon name=classicon_evoker_preservation color=c13 inline=true size=medium type=round][/icon] [color=evoker]Best Preservation Evoker Healing Priority and Rotation[/color][/h2]
[pad]

Both Preservation hero trees are extremely good so we'll look through the playstyle of each. In raid, both trees play very similarly with some minor differences in nuance and where your power is allocated. In Mythic+, the playstyles diverge a little more.



[center]
[wrapper width=70%]
[box border=true]

sections.heading: Flameshaper Raid
sections.body:
[h2 toc=false type=bar][icon name=inv_shadowflames_wave size=medium type=round color=c13 inline=true][/icon] [color=evoker]Flameshaper Raid[/color][/h2]
[/div]
[wrapper width=850px]

[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1265286.png alt="Echo, the Heart of Preservation"]

Preservation has a unique [spell=364343] mechanic where two of your spells ([spell=364343] and [spell=373861]) put [spell=364343] buffs on allies. The next spell you cast on[i] any[/i] target will consume [b]all [/b][spell=364343] buffs you have out and duplicate whatever spell you cast to all of them. 
[ul][li]If you Echo target [color=venthyr]A[/color], and then cast [spell=360995] on target [color=night-fae]B[/color] then both [color=venthyr]A[/color] and [color=night-fae]B[/color] will get a [spell=360995] heal and any associated effects.[/li]
[li]If you put five [spell=364343] buffs out with [spell=373861] then press [spell=367364], then [b]all five[/b] of them will get a [spell=367364] heal-over-time effect. [/li]
[/ul]

 
[html]
<video src="https://i.imgur.com/o8mC7OW.mp4" autoplay loop> </video>
[/html]
You'll get used to this quickly but I highly recommend logging in and casting a few Echoes around town to get used to how it works. This mechanic gives us superb flexibility in our healing style since we can prepare for damage by putting out [spell=364343] buffs and then consume them with a range of different spells depending on the situation we're in.


[toggler id=echoAdvanced hidden]Tell me more about Echo[icon name=ui_profession_inscription size=small type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/toggler]
[div id=echoAdvanced hidden]
Echo also copies all extra talents you have for the spell that you consume them with. If you [spell=367364], then they will all:
[ul][li]Heal for 15% of the damage they took recently ([spell=378196]).[/li]
[li]Receive 10% more healing from you in the future ([spell=376239]).[/li]
[li]Give you a 15% chance each of proccing [spell=369297].[/li]
[/ul]
We're going to cover which spell you should [spell=364343] later in this section, but you can see the potential. The only effect that does not [spell=364343] is [spell=373270] which is now limited to one target. [spell=364343] buffs also won't be consumed by [spell=355913] - only [spell=361469], [spell=360995], [spell=367364] and [spell=355936] - your core healing spells.

You'll often put out quite a few [spell=364343] buffs at a time before consuming them. This is sometimes referred to as a "Ramp" - a build-up of buffs before a big payoff phase where you heal a lot of people at once with one of your best spells.



[/div]
[pad]
[pad]

[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1265309.png alt="Priority - Emphasize Short Cooldowns"]
Now that you know how [spell=364343] works, we can discuss what other abilities we'll be casting a lot and how the rotation all fits together. There are two key components to preservation healing:
[ul][li][spell=364343] and the spells you will consume them with.[/li]
[li]Your short cooldown spells. Cast [spell=373861] as often as possible, and [spell=355936] just after consuming your [spell=364343] buffs. They are expensive but do more than enough healing to justify it. [span display-options=flameshaper]As Flameshaper, we'll keep one [spell=355936] charge on cooldown at all times and use both when we're in danger.[/span][/li]
[/ul]

[minor-heading]Cast these often[/minor-heading]
[table][tr][td]
[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=373861 text="On CD"]
[rt-step=355936 text="Often" ]
   [rt-step-group=360995 text="See Below" display-options="chronowarden"]]
     [rt-sup=431657]
  [/rt-step-group]
[/rotation-timeline]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[minor-heading]Do this in between[/minor-heading]
[table][tr][td]
[rotation-timeline]

    [rt-step-group=355913]
        [rt-sup=369297]
    [/rt-step-group]
    [rt-step-group=364343]]
        [rt-sup text="Essence"]
    [/rt-step-group]
[rt-step=1256581 text="When damage"]
[rt-step=431442 text="On Boss" display-options="chronowarden"]
[rt-step=361469 text="On Boss" display-options="flameshaper"]
[/rotation-timeline]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[div display-options="chronowarden"]
[b]Quick Chronowarden Priority List[/b]
[ol]
[li]Cast [spell=373861] on cooldown.[/li]
[li]Cast [spell=355936] often. Cast it after you have consumed [spell=364343] buffs to avoid consuming them with [spell=355936].[/li]
[li]Cast [spell=360995] shortly after a [spell=1256577] cast with 0-2 Echoes out. - [span class=tip tooltip=VEChrono][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
[li]Cast [spell=355913] if you have an [spell=369297].[/li]
[li]Cast [spell=364343] if you have Essence available and either no [spell=369297] buff or you are at two stacks of [spell=1242031].[/li]
[li]Consume [spell=364343] buffs with [spell=1256581] (common) or [spell=360995] (rare).[/li]
[li]Cast [spell=361469] on the boss to farm [spell=369297]s and contribute a little damage. You get a large mana refund if you cast it on an enemy instead of an ally.[/li]
[/ol]
[/div]

[div display-options="flameshaper"]
[b]Quick Flameshaper Priority List[/b]
[ol]
[li]Cast [spell=373861] on cooldown.[/li]
[li]Keep one [spell=355936] charge on cooldown. Cast the second when there is dangerous boss damage. [/li]
[li]Cast [spell=355913] if you have an [spell=369297].[/li]
[li]Cast [spell=364343] if you have Essence available and either no [spell=369297] buff or you are at two Twin Echo stacks.[/li]
[li]Consume [spell=364343] buffs with [spell=1256581] (common) or [spell=355936] (rare).[/li]
[li]Cast [spell=361469] on the boss to farm [spell=369297]s and contribute a little damage.[/li]
[/ol]
[/div]
[pad]



[toggler id=echoBlossom hidden]Explain Echo vs Emerald Blossom [icon name=ui_profession_inscription size=small type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/toggler]
[div id=echoBlossom hidden]
[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/images/wow/icons/large/ability_evoker_emeraldblossom.jpg] [b]VS [/b][img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/images/wow/icons/large/ability_evoker_echo.jpg]
The [spell=1242031] talent incentivizes [spell=355913] usage by giving us a double [spell=364343] on our next cast if we do. [spell=355913] is also expensive, both in terms of mana and essence. However, [spell=369297] removes both of those costs. If you have two bursts you can cast two [spell=355913] in a row and then your next two [spell=364343] casts will each cleave to a nearby ally.

[b]Therefore, we should always cast [spell=355913] when we have an [spell=369297] unless we already have two stacks of [spell=1242031]. If we do, cast Echo.  [/b]

[b][color=kyrian][b]Advanced Tip:[/b] After pressing [spell=370537] or [spell=359816], it is ok to press [spell=355913] even at 2 stacks of [spell=1242031] while in the [spell=1242745] buff window. This is due to the extra [spell=355936] healing giving us massive [spell=444088] value.[/color][/b]
[/div][pad]

[toggler id=echoChoice hidden]Explain when to consume Echo with which spell [icon name=ui_profession_inscription size=small type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/toggler]
[div id=echoChoice hidden]
[div display-options="chronowarden"]
[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/images/wow/icons/large/ability_evoker_spiritbloom.jpg] [b]VS [/b][img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/images/wow/icons/large/ability_evoker_rescue.jpg]
There are two primary choices: [spell=1256581] and [spell=360995]. [spell=1256581] will be your primary choice but it is a proc so it won't always be available. Your core play pattern will revolve around farming [spell=1256581] (each [spell=364343] and [spell=355913] has a 20% chance to proc it) and then consuming your [spell=364343] buffs with it. If you get unlucky, it is ok to consume with [spell=367364] in a pinch. Ideal play includes playing around your [spell=355936] cooldown, since pressing [spell=355936] guarantees you a [spell=1256577] proc.

[spell=360995]'s niche is large healing absorbs since the amount it heals the primary [spell=364343] targets is higher than [spell=1256577] (which heals for a lot via its cleave and flow-on effects instead).

[b][color=evoker]Remember that [spell=1256577] also puts a full strength [spell=367364] on the target with all associated effects! It is just a [spell=367364] with a massive up-front multi-target heal attached.[/color][/b]

[/div]
[div display-options="flameshaper"]
[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/images/wow/icons/large/ability_evoker_spiritbloom.jpg] [b]VS [/b][img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/images/wow/icons/large/ability_evoker_dreambreath.jpg]
There are two primary choices: [spell=1256581] and [spell=355936]. [spell=1256581] will be your primary choice. Your core play pattern will revolve around getting a guaranteed proc from [spell=355936] and then consuming your [spell=364343] buffs with it.

[spell=355936]'s niche is for targets that will take sustained damage for quite a while (like a dangerous DoT or healing absorb). You are able to put two [spell=355936] HoTs on that target and then [spell=360995] them to heal for a lot and proc [spell=444088] twice.

[b][color=evoker]Remember that [spell=1256577] also puts a full strength [spell=367364] on the target with all associated effects! It is just a [spell=367364] with a massive up-front multi-target heal attached.[/color][/b]

[/div]
[/div][pad]
[/div]


[toggler id=manaIssues hidden]I'm having mana trouble [icon name=ui_profession_inscription size=small type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/toggler]
[div id=manaIssues hidden]
Mana is a conundrum as Preservation because our most expensive spell ([spell=373861]) is also our most powerful. The best way to manage mana on Preservation, is to line up your casts better with the bosses damage pattern. It's very common to see players drop 50% of their mana in the opening minute of the fight during Bloodlust and to get very poor returns out of the spend. Even in Mythic raid, you can identify areas of the fight where you don't need to be casting [spell=373861] on cooldown. I would not recommend cutting any buttons (like [spell=360995]) out of your rotation entirely. 

It's also possible to take the [spell=372233] talent, which gives mana return on [spell=356995] cast. If taken, you will use either Essence or [spell=369297] on [spell=356995] during downtime to recover. Whether to take [spell=372233] or not is discussed more in the talents section of the guide, but you're only trading 2% healing or so to take it. Just this on a fight by fight basis but try and improve how you use your existing mana before you try to add more.

[/div][pad]

[h4 type=bar]Further Explanation[/h4]
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right]There is no set number of [spell=364343] buffs you should aim to put out before consuming them. Your gameplay will mostly revolve around a cycle where you put out as many as possible before dangerous damage hits and then consume them all at once. If you have resources available, then you should spend them. [hr][/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right]While you should practice casting Echo with Twin Echoes and Emerald Blossom otherwise, it is ok if you make some mistakes. So long as you are spending Essence Bursts, your choice of spell won't overly destroy your HPS.[hr][/li]
[/ul]


[/wrapper]
[/tab]
[tab name="Mythic+ Healing" icon=ability_evoker_rescue]
[pad]
[div display-options=chronowarden]

[h2 toc=false type=bar][icon name=ability_evoker_aspectsfavorbronze size=medium type=round color=c13 inline=true][/icon] [color=evoker]Chronowarden Mythic+[/color][/h2]
[/div]
[div display-options=flameshaper]

sections.heading: Flameshaper Mythic+
sections.body:
[h2 toc=false type=bar][icon name=inv_shadowflames_wave size=medium type=round color=c13 inline=true][/icon] [color=evoker]Flameshaper Mythic+[/color][/h2]
[/div]
[wrapper width=850px]

[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1265286.png alt="Echo, the Heart of Preservation"]

Preservation has a unique [spell=364343] mechanic where two of your spells ([spell=364343] and [spell=373861]) put [spell=364343] buffs on allies. The next spell you cast on[i] any[/i] party member will consume [b]all [/b][spell=364343] buffs you have out and duplicate whatever spell you cast to all of them. 
[ul][li]If you [spell=364343] target [color=venthyr]A[/color], and then cast [spell=360995] on target [color=night-fae]B[/color] then both [color=venthyr]A[/color] and [color=night-fae]B[/color] will get a [spell=360995] heal and any associated effects. [b]This is primarily how we will use [spell=364343] casts in Mythic+[/b].[/li]
[li]If you put five [spell=364343] buffs out with [spell=373861] then press [spell=367364], then [b]all five[/b] of them will get a [spell=367364] heal-over-time effect. [b]This is primarily how we will use [spell=373861] in Mythic+.[/b][/li]
[/ul]

 
[html]
<video src="https://i.imgur.com/o8mC7OW.mp4" autoplay loop> </video>
[/html]


[toggler id=echoAdvanced2 hidden]Tell me more about Echo[icon name=ui_profession_inscription size=small type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/toggler]
[div id=echoAdvanced2 hidden]
Echo also copies all extra talents you have for the spell that you consume them with. If you [spell=367364], then they will all:
[ul][li]Heal for 15% of the damage they took recently ([spell=378196]).[/li]
[li]Receive 10% more healing from you in the future ([spell=376239]).[/li]
[li]Give you a 15% chance each of proccing [spell=369297].[/li]
[/ul]
We're going to cover which spell you should [spell=364343] later in this section, but you can see the potential. The only effect that does not [spell=364343] is [spell=373270] which is now limited to one target. [spell=364343] buffs also won't be consumed by [spell=355913] - only [spell=361469], [spell=360995], [spell=367364] and [spell=355936] - your core healing spells.

You'll often put out quite a few [spell=364343] buffs at a time before consuming them. This is sometimes referred to as a "Ramp" - a build-up of buffs before a big payoff phase where you heal a lot of people at once with one of your best spells.

[/div]
[pad]
[pad]
[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1265669.png]

Mythic+ involves a mix of healing unavoidable damage, and mistakes your group might make. The former will get more difficult as you climb key levels, and the latter often gets easier as player skill improves. Preservation excels at damage you know is coming but has fewer responses to sharp damage on a single player. Let's look at what we have available to us:

[minor-heading]Cast Combo on Cooldown - [spell=367364] Uptime[/minor-heading]
[table][tr][td]
[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=373861]
[rt-step=366155]
[/rotation-timeline]
[/td][/tr][/table]

This gives you a 100% uptime on the [spell=367364] buff on the entire group and a very frequent shield on everyone.

[toggler id=reversionAdvanced hidden]Why is this important[icon name=ui_profession_inscription size=small type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/toggler]
[div id=reversionAdvanced hidden]
[spell=367364] coverage puts a 10% healing buff on your entire group ([spell=376239]), covers small incidental damage they'll take via the HoT and in Midnight will also give them a damage reduction effect. Some of these do not scale with the power of the [spell=364343] buff you consume which makes [spell=367364] a uniquely good spell to combine with [spell=373861] (which puts out weaker [spell=364343] buffs). These will also give you a chance to proc [spell=443177] - a good damage or healing effect.
[/div]

[minor-heading]Heavier Damage - [spell=360995][/minor-heading]
[html]
<video src="https://i.imgur.com/Z3s71Xt.mp4" autoplay loop> </video>
[/html]
[table][tr][td]
[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=364343]
[rt-step=364343]
[rt-step=364343]
[rt-step=360995]
[/rotation-timeline]
[/td][/tr][/table]

When heavy damage is coming up you can use your [spell=364343] spell to put larger [spell=364343] buffs on your party. You can usually prioritize two DPS in your in your party plus yourself since the tank is not usually vulnerable to the same type of AoE damage as the rest of your party. Then, cast [spell=360995] on whoever you didn't [spell=364343]. The [spell=360995] cast is copied to your three [spell=364343] targets and all four of you will get a massive heal and a solid 8-second heal-over-time effect afterwards. 

[pad]

[minor-heading]Fitting in your other spells[/minor-heading]
Those will make up quite a lot of your healing but we have a few more useful spells too. Here are some common scenarios where they'll be useful:
[ul][li][spell=355936]: Key Cast. Cast on cooldown at rank 1 if damage is low to moderate. Cast at rank 3 if you require a burst heal.[/li]
[li][spell=357208]: Key Cast. Massive AoE damage ability that'll also heal the party for a lot. Cast at rank 3.[/li]
[li][spell=357170]: Superb damage reduction for a single target. Low cooldown so use this regularly.[/li]
[li][spell=374227]: Cast before AoE damage to reduce how much damage it does. You'll generally need to play through a dungeon a few times to pick out useful spots for it. [/li]
[/ul]
We also bring quite a few powerful healing cooldowns that we'll discuss further down the page.

[minor-heading]Spot Healing - Fixing Mistakes[/minor-heading]
Sometimes a single target will take a lot of damage at once. It could be the tank, or it could be from a missed interrupt. We'll respond to those types of events by casting [spell=367364] on the target immediately, or if we think we have an extra GCD we can Echo -> [spell=367364]. We're taking advantage of [spell=378196] which heals back a portion of the damage they just took. We have two charges of [spell=367364] so it won't interrupt your [spell=373861] -> [spell=367364] plan from above. If they require more healing afterwards we'll use one of [spell=360995], [spell=357170] or even a [spell=361469] if we're out of everything else.

[/wrapper]

[/tab]
[tab name="Pre-Combat Checks" icon=inv_misc_paperbundle02b]

[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/1265740.png]
Here's what you should do before every raid or dungeon:
[ul][li]Cast [spell=364342] (our raid buff) - every pull.[/li]
[li](Raid) Make sure [spell=369459] is active on another healer. Your highest HPS ally is a good target.[/li]
[li]Make sure you have a Flask on - applied every 1-2 hours.[/li]
[li]Make sure you have a Food buff - either every pull or every hour depending on the food.[/li]
[li]Make sure you have a [item=243734] on your weapon - applied every two hours.[/li]
[li](Optional) Apply a [item=259085] on - every pull. Can be expensive so lowest priority.[/li]
[li]Cast [spell=373861] a few seconds before you pull. It'll give you some [spell=364343] buffs to start the fight with. [/li]
[/ul]

You can read about the best Flask and food buff to use in the [url guide=17756]Preservation Consumables guide[/url].

[/tab]

[/tabs]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=evoker][icon name=ability_evoker_rewind type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon] Preservation Evoker Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]
Preservation has access to some of the most powerful healing cooldowns in the game. Let's go through them and discuss where we might use them. Aim to pre-plan cooldowns as often as possible. Avoid scenarios where you're saving them "just in case", since this can cost you a lot of Mana through a fight and will increase the chance your raid suffers a death. Layer your raid's defensive cooldowns over the most dangerous moments of each fight to ensure you're covered.
[pad]
[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Stasis" icon=ability_evoker_stasis]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_evoker_stasis type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon][color=evoker] Stasis\u200e [/color][/h3]

[spell=370537] lets you store and then re-cast three spells, which means you can capture high value cooldowns like [spell=355936] and [spell=373861] and cast them again in a big healing burst. [spell=370537] can be quite intimidating to use as a beginner since it stores 3 spells for a subsequent, later use of them. This rewards pre-emptive, planned use since it takes time to store all three spells and you'll need the spells off cooldown too.

[h3][icon name=ability_evoker_stasis color=c13 inline=true size=medium type=round][/icon] How to play with [spell=370537][/h3]

[h4]How it works[/h4]
[ul][li][spell=370537] spells have no cost, no cooldown, and spells will trigger in the order they were stored.[/li]
[li]For targeted spells, [spell=370537] will send the duplicated spell at the [b]same target[/b]. For spells without a target such as [spell=355936], [spell=370537] will send the duplicated spell in whichever direction you are currently facing. [/li]
[li]Empowered spells will cast at whatever Rank the original was cast at.[/li]
[li]Doesn't work on major cooldowns like [spell=359816], [spell=363534], and so on. It also only counts helpful spells, and thus can't be used as a DPS cooldown.[/li]
[/ul]
You have quite a bit of flexibility over which specific spells you [spell=370537], but you'll want to aim for high value ones where possible. 

[h4]Stasis Combos[/h4]
[h5]The Standard[/h5]
This is the format most [spell=370537] combos will take:
[table][tr][td]
[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=370537]
[rt-step=355936 text="Rank X"]
[rt-step=373861]
[rt-step=1256581 text="?"]]
[rt-step=370537 text="Release"]
[/rotation-timeline]
[/td][/tr][/table]

The [spell=1256577] here is a flex-slot and many spells can situationally be included here instead:

[ul][li] Flameshaper might want to store a second [spell=355936] (optimal, but requires you to wait until both charges are available)[/li]
[li]You might store an [spell=355913], or Echo cast. This lets you save the [spell=1256577] charge generated by the [spell=355936].[/li]
[/ul]

Mostly just make sure you are storing 1x [spell=373861] and at least 1x [spell=355936].


[h5]Chronowarden Coverage Combo[/h5]
This combo maximises how many [spell=364343] buffs you can get out on the raid. Raid Chronowarden will also combine [spell=370537] with [spell=370553] so we will have significant Haste via [spell=431695]. You might have to wait a moment for the second [spell=373861] to come off cooldown but it'll be short and it's worth it.

[table][tr][td]
[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=355936 text="Rank 1"]
[rt-step=370537]
[rt-step=373861]
[rt-step=364343]
[rt-step=373861]
[rt-step=370537 text="Release"]
[/rotation-timeline]
[/td][/tr][/table]


[h5]Pre-pull Cheese[/h5]
If there's a key damage event early in the fight it is possible to store three [spell=373861] in your [spell=370537] before the pull and then release it right before the damage event. The shield will absorb a ton and you'll have [spell=364343] on the entire raid. It's also possible to do this mid-fight but it's a little impractical since you'll spend 16-20 seconds doing nothing while [spell=373861] cools down.

[table][tr][td]
[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=370537]
[rt-step=373861]
[rt-step=373861]
[rt-step=373861]
[rt-step=370537 text="Release"]
[/rotation-timeline]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[h5]Mass Dispel[/h5]
[spell=374251]s removes almost all dispellable debuffs and Bleeds from a target, but doesn't go on cooldown if it doesn't remove anything. That means we can store three in our [spell=370537] in advance and fully clear the entire group with it. This is niche, but worth having in your back pocket.

[table][tr][td]
[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step=370537]
[rt-step=374251]
[rt-step=374251]
[rt-step=374251]
[rt-step=370537 text="Release"]
[/rotation-timeline]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[spell=370537] will require a lot of practice to master, and don't expect to play it perfectly at first. Once you're in the habit of using it to prepare for and handle high incoming damage, you'll find it's something you can't live without.

[/tab]
[tab name="Dream Flight" icon=ability_evoker_dreamflight]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_evoker_dreamflight type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon][color=evoker] Dream Flight\u200e [/color][/h3]
[spell=359816] is a large area AoE heal that'll send you in your chosen direction for 10-50 yards, healing everyone beneath you. It's a high-impact spell on a fairly reasonable cooldown, so you'll want to fit in as many uses as you can. It also adds a lengthy HoT to each target. [b]Aim for a stacked group.[/b] 

[spell=359816] also applies a large absorb to you while you're in the air (equal to your health bar) which means you should be quite safe. This is removed the instant you land.

[/tab]
[tab name="Rewind" icon=ability_evoker_rewind]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_evoker_rewind type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon][color=evoker] Rewind [/color][/h3]
Arguably the strongest healing cooldown in the game and certainly among the top 3. [spell=363534] applies a 5 second HoT based on 33% of damage taken in the 5 seconds prior to you hitting the button. It also has a minimum value attached to it, and is doubled in dungeon content. [b]You'll want to line this up with the most dangerous moments of every fight.[/b]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Evoker Deep Dives
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Evoker Deep Dives" type=bar][icon name=classicon_evoker_preservation color=c13 inline=true size=medium type=round][/icon] Evoker Deep Dives[/h2]
In this section we'll cover different aspects of the spec in a little more depth. These are all fairly optional, but can be useful in increasing your overall understanding of the class. If you're brand new to the spec, I'd advise revisiting this section after getting some practice.
[br]

[tabs name="Deep Dives"]

[tab name="Overcoming a 30 yard range"]
[h3]Overcoming a 30 yard Range[/h3]
Preservation is unique in being the only Healing spec in the game with a reduced 30 yard range. This means that we're able to heal 56% of the area a standard healing spec can, and 44% of the area a Restoration Druid can. The impact of this varies a lot on a fight-by-fight basis - on some fights you'll barely notice it, and in others it'll be a major hindrance. Some tips to play around this limitation include:
[ul][li]Stand centrally wherever a fight permits. [/li]
[li]Set your mobility buttons to good keybinds and use them often. [spell=358267], [spell=360995], [spell=370665], and [spell=374227] are all powerful, and between all of them you should have an answer to most movement requirements. Use [spell=358267] as your go-to, since it has the fewest restrictions. [/li]
[li]Adjust and update your planned positioning in between pulls. It isn't always possible to be in a great place, but you can at least be in a good one.[/li]
[li]If you're about to run out of range of a priority target, put a HoT like [spell=355936] or [spell=367364] on them, or an [spell=364343] that you can consume later from any range.[/li][/ul]

In Mythic+, you're likely to find it an occasional annoyance. You might want to consider telling any group members to stay a little closer than they might otherwise so that they are easier to hit with [spell=355936].
[/tab]
[/tabs]

[hr]
Our Preservation Evoker guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Preservation Evoker guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page.
[pad]


[pad]
[hr]
